findings.finding: The three rev12 schemas now share the D0 regularity domain byte-identically (probe d0_equal_raw=true and d0_normalized_equal_all_three=true) and share the numeric (s,delta,norm) core (probe shared_regularity_numeric_contract=true: same default, s > 5/2, delta in (1/2,1), same weighted-Sobolev spaces modulo the parenthetical '(weighted Sobolev)'). Strict data_class blocks are nevertheless not identical: F1 vs F2a and F1 vs F2b differ in ['adm_mass','asymptotic_decay','diffeo_quotient','excluded_data','gauge','regularity_class'], and F2a vs F2b differ in ['adm_mass'] even after annotation stripping. F1 is the only schema carrying data_class.excluded_data; the adm_mass field sets differ (F1 has rigidity, F2a has locator, F2b has locator plus hypotheses_reconciliation); the remaining four are prose variants. On the gate's literal wording ('no single frozen data class (s,delta,norm) is shared by F1/F2a/F2b') the shared D0 plus equal numeric contract satisfies the criterion; on a strict byte-identity reading it does not, and this finding then becomes blocking. Recorded as a major advisory to the G-FORM owner (lead-audit verification astra-life03-verify-gform) and to lead-formulation, not as a hard failure of F1-local conformance.
